As an Indo Western competitive dance team, we aim to provide students an opportunity to learn, perform, and share South Asian inspired and fusion dance styles while forming community, inclusivity, and personal growth.

name: Champaign-Urbana Business and Engineering Consulting
description: Champaign-Urbana Business and Engineering Consulting (CUBE) is a non-profit consulting organization with a talented group of students who work together on meaningful projects for local businesses.We are committed to Growth, Impact, Leadership, and Diversity. We work with local clients, with a focus on impacting the Champaign-Urbana and Chicagoland area to develop hands-on experience and opportunities to create a lasting impact and have a diverse portfolio of over 100 projects accumulated throughout the past 10 years from business, engineering, and design sectors.

name: Character Creation Hub
description: CCH aims to provide a place where students can create original characters/stories and share them with people of similar interests. We strive to promote collaboration and individual commissions to hone our skills and inspire each other.

name: Cheese Club At UIUC
description: The Cheese Club at UIUC serves to promote the cultural and educational significance of cheese, to introduce students to the diverse cheese-making traditions around the world, foster appreciation and understanding through meetings, tastings, and events, and create an accessible space for learning and collaboration, all in the belief that cheese has the power to connect people across cultures and deepen our understanding of the world.

name: Chem E Cube UIUC
description: Chem E Cube UIUC serves to foster innovation and creativity in chemical engineering while building and demonstrating a 1 cubic foot plant prototype that addresses an annual problem statement.

name: Chi Epsilon Civil Engineering Honor Society
description: Chi Epsilon (XE) is the National Civil Engineering Honor Society in the United States, dedicated to recognizing students who embody the principles of scholarship, character, practicality, and sociability in the civil engineering profession. Founded on May 20, 1922, at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, it emerged from the efforts of two groups of civil engineering students who independently petitioned to establish an honorary fraternity. Since then, Chi Epsilon has grown to 147 chapters nationwide, with over 125,000 initiated members. The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign chapt

name: Chi Iota Chapter of the Fraternity of Phi Gamma Delta
description: Phi Gamma Delta unites men in enduring friendships, stimulates the pursuit of knowledge, and builds courageous leaders who serve the world with the best that is in them.

name: Chi Omega
description: Chi Omega Fraternity is an intergenerational women’s organization forever committed to our founding purposes: Friendship, Personal integrity, Service to others, Academic excellence and intellectual pursuits, Community and campus involvement, Personal and career development.

name: Chi Psi Fraternity
description: A family of gentlemen in pursuit of strong brotherhood and academic greatness.

name: Chi Sigma Tau National Fraternity, Inc.
description: Realizing that all young men need someone to look up to for guidance, we the Brothers of Chi Sigma Tau National Fraternity, Inc. have come together as an Asian Interest Fraternity to promote this idea through a program of mentorship by promoting academic excellence, leadership development, cultural awareness and social events within our membership upon the basis of brotherhood.

name: Child Life Association
description: The Child Life Association serves to provide information and events relating to the child life field and becoming a certified child life specialist.

name: Chinese Engineering Students Association (CESA)
description: UIUC CESA is a non-profit organization established by Chinese engineering students. Since its founding, CESA has been committed to providing academic and life support to Chinese students. While initially formed as a communication platform for engineering students, our group members come from various colleges and majors, emphasizing diversity rather than limiting participation based on majors or grades.

name: Chinese Language Association for International Development
description: Founded in UIUC in 2015, CLAID is a student organization committed to spreading and appreciating Chinese culture through inclusive, beginner-friendly opportunities open to students of all backgrounds, majors, and experience levels. Our goal is to foster a welcoming community for those interested in Chinese language and culture, bridge the gap between Chinese international and domestic students, and create meaningful opportunities for students to learn, connect, and engage with one another.

name: Chinese Students and Scholars Association
description: The Chinese Students and Scholars Association (CSSA) is the official organization for overseas Chinese students at UIUC. We aim at providing resources and necessary help for Chinese students studying at UIUC. The purpose(s) of this organization shall be promoting intellectual, social, and cultural interactions among Chinese students as well as the U of I community. At the same time, we devote ourselves to facilitate the relationship and communication between Chinese community and the U of I family. Home to the international Chinese students, we strive to engage our own community with the local

name: Chinese Theatre Group
description: 1. We aim to establish an efficient management system to facilitate the smooth functioning of the community. Through a diverse range of activities, including workshops and hands-on experiences in every aspect of theatre production, we prioritize practical learning. These activities will not only be open to the public but also designed to attract individuals interested in theatre, fostering a broader understanding of the art form. 2. Beyond educational objectives, we seek to enrich the college experience for our members and the public by incorporating social events, outings, and a supportive co

name: CHOOM
description: The purpose of the CHOOM* Club is to gather passionate Cpop and Kpop dancers and spread our love for dancing by practicing and performing Cpop and Kpop dances to flourish and add diversity to the UIUC community.

name: Chords @ Illini
description: Chords @ Illini’s mission is to bring together guitar enthusiasts of all skill levels to practice, collaborate, perform, and share a passion for guitar music.

name: Christ Community
description: The purpose of Christ Community is to multiply disciples of Jesus. We seek to help students grow in their faith and live a life committed to God’s purposes in the world.

name: Christian Business Association
description: The Christian Business Association exists to build Christian fellowship amongst business and business-related students, connect students to full-time roles in Christian and Non-Profit fields, and build strong Christian ethics that they can take into the workforce.

name: Christian Campus Fellowship UIUC
description: The CCF is a community dedicated to advancing study of Christianity and religion through research and academic inquiry. CCF offers an opportunity to build a deeper understanding of faith helping students grow both spiritually and intellectually to develop skills necessary for a potential future in pastorship, chaplaincy, and religious scholarship. We also discipleship and outreach to help believers to grow spiritually and serve their communities. Through open dialogue and academic exploration, CCF prepares students both theologically and practically to make a meaningful impact in religious and

name: Christian Law Students Association
description: The purpose of the Christian Law Students Association is to provide a community for students seeking to learn more about Christianity and to grow in their faith through meaningful fellowship, service, prayer, and Bible study. CLSA supports the spiritual lives of law students who are Christians or are interested in learning more about Christianity.

name: Christian Literature Club
description: Christian Literature Club serves to introduce well-known spiritual people who contribute a lot to Christianity. Our club welcomes all students with or without religious backgrounds, giving them a good insight of Christian riches. Through wonderful spiritual work, vision, and different interpretations of the Bible, club members will not only further understand the scripture, but also earn both personal and corporate experience of the word of God through reading their paragon of life and faith. Our club offers: 1. An opportunity for members to enhance their writing and literary appreciation by c

name: Christian Medical and Dental Association
description: The Christian Medical & Dental Association (CMDA) chapter at UIUC serves to educate, encourage, and equip healthcare students and professionals to glorify God through medicine. We seek to foster a welcoming community where Christians can grow in faith, worship, and fellowship while navigating healthcare through a Christ-centered lens. We also strive to create an open and inviting space for those who are curious about God, encouraging thoughtful discussion, compassion, service, and faithful engagement with the challenges of healthcare.

name: Christians on Campus
description: The purpose of CoC shall be to provide an opportunity for students interested in the Christian faith to become acquainted and related to other Christians in and outside of the club, to pursue the Christian faith and study the Bible with other students, and to participate in community outreach.

name: CIMED Family Medicine Interest Group
description: CIMED Family Medicine Interest Group (FMIG) serves to promote interest in and increase awareness of family medicine as a medical specialty among medical students. The organization aims to provide students with opportunities for professional development, mentorship, networking, community service, and clinical exposure within the field of family medicine. name: Circle K International-UIUC Chapter
description: Developing college and university students into a global network of responsible citizens and leaders with a lifelong commitment to service.

name: Circular Fashion Expo (CFE)
description: Through exhibitions, events, and educational initiatives, CFE strives to raise awareness about the environmental and social impact of fashion while fostering a community of like-minded individuals dedicated to creating positive change.

name: Classic Literature Book Club
description: the Classic Literature Book Club serves to create a welcoming community for individuals who are interested in reading and discussing both traditional and modern works of classic literature, not limited to but primarily in the form of books. (This definition of classic literature is not to be confused with the Greco-Roman classical studies).

name: Climate and Meteorological Association of Students
description: CliMAS is committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and thriving graduate student community to aid in the Department of Climate, Meteorology and Atmospheric Sciences mission of conducting world-class research, providing a world-class education, and guiding students to be leaders and exemplary citizens.

name: Climbing Club at UIUC
description: The purpose of the Climbing Club is to unite climbers, introduce climbing to new people, promote safe climbing and environmental stewardship, and to purchase and maintain gear for club use.

name: Climbing Illini Competitive Team at UIUC
description: The Climbing Illini - UIUC Competitive Team serves to provide a pathway to competitive climbing at the collegiate level through USA Climbing as well as provide climbers with guidance on how to improve their climbing and competition strategy.

name: Club Insecta
description: Club Insecta serves to educate, understand, nurture, and inform individuals about insects and other animals and provide a safe environment for those with interest in insects.

name: Club Pickleball at the University of Illinois
description: Club Pickleball at the University of Illinois serves to bring together students at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign to play and enjoy the sport of pickleball in a competitive and recreational environment.

name: Club Tennis
description: The purpose of this organization is to allow members to play tennis in a safe, respectful, and welcoming environment.

name: Clubs Communities
description: “To support all students in finding and fostering their community—because we need each other.”

name: Co-Ed Flag Football at Illinois
description: Co-Ed Flag Football at Illinois serves to provide a fun, welcoming, and inclusive space for students of all skill levels to learn and develop flag football skills. Students will stay physically active while building meaningful relationships. Unlike intramural teams that focus on competition, this organization focuses on skill development, growth, and community while giving a fun alternative way to exercise. Through weekly practices, drills, and friendly scrimmages, members will have the chance to learn flag football fundamentals, stay healthy, and make new friends in a supportive environment.

name: CodeRed
description: CodeRed at UIUC serves as a welcoming space for people who are passionate about bringing period equity to our local community. Our organization strives to educate students on menstrual health topics and unite advocates across campus.

name: College of Law Labor and Employment Law Society at the University of Illinois
description: The first major purpose this organization will serve shall be to inform and educate students at the College of Law about both the fields of labor & employment law, provide networking opportunities for students, and offer perspectives on the major career opportunities in these fields. This shall be done through, but will not be limited to, informational meetings and seminars involving guest speakers within the fields of labor & employment law. ii.) The other major purpose this organization will serve will be to promote working-class solidarity within the Champaign-Urbana community and beyond. O

name: College of Nursing at Urbana Urban Health Program
description: The UHP serves to provide opportunities for early exposure to nursing education and careers for prospective students from traditionally underrepresented groups. To provide academic enrichment opportunities for the success and retention of all students.

name: College Republicans at UIUC
description: To support the America First agenda through activism, service, and public awareness; to develop future leaders of the Republican party.

name: Colombian Student Association at the University of Illinois
description: The Colombian Student Association exists to celebrate and share Colombian culture, build an inclusive community among Colombian, Colombian-American, and allied students, and support members’ academic and professional growth through cultural events, mentorship, workshops, service, and partnerships across campus and the Champaign-Urbana community.

name: Coloring Hours UIUC
description: Our mission as Coloring Hours UIUC is to provide students with a stress-free environment where students can decompress and be free to explore their creative side while caring for their mental health and action of self-care.

name: Combat Robotics
description: The purpose of Combat Robotics shall be to provide, through the medium of robotics, an opportunity to practice a variety of engineering, teamwork, and leadership skills as well as network with others who share similar interests, with the joint goals of educating and preparing members for their professional career and spreading STEM awareness throughout the community.

name: Combating Screen Time Club
description: The CSTC serves to foster a community of students that encourage each other to recognize screen time habits; become more responsible with digital technologies and social media use; and develop healthy habits that combat contemporary screen time dependencies.

name: Competitive Illini Squash Club
description: We aim to cultivate a highly competitive squash team at UIUC, dedicated to participating in structured training, development, and intercollegiate play. We will select committed members through try outs and prepare a final roster (9 for the club sport) to represent UIUC in collegiate tournaments and competitions cross the country

name: Competitive Super Smash Bros. Club
description: To create a welcoming and inclusive local community. To host engaging and exciting experiences for the regional Super Smash Bros. community. To promote and foster a healthy competitive environment for players that attend our events.

name: Competitive Taekwondo Club
description: The Competitive Taekwondo Club serves to train its members in a rigorous team environment exclusively under the World Taekwondo style in competitive sparring, poomsae, and demonstration, representing the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign at a collegiate level.

name: Concept Connect
description: The purpose of CC is to: 1. Provide academic support and resources to students. 2. Foster a sense of fraternity and mentorship among members. 3. Facilitate campus integration and support for new and existing students. 4. Encourage active participation and engagement in campus life.

name: Conch Shell Mental Support
description: The purpose of the CONCH SHELL MENTAL SUPPORT shall be: To provide mental health support for Chinese students abroad through offering emotional support To raise attention and awareness of mental problems and the science of Psychology through events and WeChat online platform To link students to campus resources based on individual needs To provide a connection to the greater student body To prepare potential Chinese students abroad for future challenges To set goals and plans for advancing the University of Illinois and its Psychology Department To promote the name and reputation of the Univer

name: Concrete Canoe at UIUC
description: The UIUC Concrete Canoe RSO serves as a student run organization that will spend approximately a semester and a half constructing and building a canoe out of concrete. Our ultimate goal is to apply and teach civil engineering principles regarding construction processes, structural design, and concrete design. In addition, UIUC Concrete Canoe serves to provide students with an opportunity to learn canoe paddling techniques and compete against other universities in races at ASCE sanctioned events.

name: Connect @ UIUC
description: Connect @ UIUC serves to form meaningful connections with RSOs and build a vast network to allow for collaboration between them. Additionally, we will reach out to all RSOs and allow our members to attend their event to learn about them and potentially join that RSO.

name: Construction Management Association of America
description: The Construction Management Association of America (CMAA) – UIUC Chapter serves as to offer students the opportunity to develop professional and technical perspectives associated with the construction management (CM) services profession while pursuing their academic programs. Student participation in CMAA events at the national or regional level provides valuable networking opportunities for future employment, and the educational programs offered at CMAA functions contribute to the early professional development of the prospective CM practitioner.

name: Consumer Economics and Finance Club (CEF Club)
description: The Consumer Economics and Finance club serves to provide students with a variety of professional development opportunities. Students expand their knowledge and skills in the Consumer Economics and Finance Club industry through professional guest speakers, workshops, and networking with other CEF student members and alums. The ultimate goal is to create an environment that prepares students for future careers

name: Contract Bridge Illini Orange
description: To build a community of card sharks and have a fun time doing it!

name: Coptic Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: Our mission is to provide a homey environment in which enriches people spiritually and socially. In addition, our mission is to interact with the school and community in a means of Evangelism.

name: Cornerstone Christian Student Fellowship
description: Cornerstone Fellowship (CCCC) serves as the student ministry of Champaign Chinese Christian Church in Champaign, IL.

name: Corporate and Business Law Association
description: The Corporate and Business Law Association strives to promote and preserve student interest in business and law, especially as they relate to each other; to infuse legal concepts into club-sponsored events and activities; and to facilitate professional growth and development.

name: Cosmetic Chemistry Club
description: The Cosmetic Chemistry Club serves to create a place where students can explore science and how it applies to their daily lives. This group will learn about how chemistry relates to commercial products in a new and more approachable manner, accessible for all levels of chemistry knowledge. Finally, we will introduce students to the industry of cosmetics.

name: Cosplay Design League
description: The Cosplay Design League serves to provide a place for students to work on and create costumes together. The Cosplay Design League will teach students about sewing, foam smithing, patternmaking, and 3D design and printing for props, armor, and costumes. The Cosplay Design League creates a social environment for people of similar interests. This organization will coordinate trips to conventions which display costume design, as well as provide a place for its members to discuss creation techniques and work as a group to produce costumes.

name: Covenant Fellowship
description: The purpose of Covenant Fellowship is to be a community where anyone can come and learn and share about the person of Jesus Christ.

name: Cover 2 Cover
description: Bring together women from all cultural backgrounds to create an environment where their love for books can be explored, challenged, and transformed through both collective and individual reading experiences. We aim to foster connections on campus while enhancing the broader community by engaging with schools, nursing homes, and hospitals.

name: Craft Bakers Union
description: The Craft Bakers Union serves to bring baking back to the realm of the trades with a two-pronged approach. First: Raising our community’s appreciation for quality ingredients, well-made equipment, and skilled labor. Second: Teaching our members how to bake well and prioritize both learning and labor in the kitchen.

name: Creative Illini
description: Creative Illini serves as A) A place for students to express their creativity through the arts to de-stress and socialize. B) Provide a community designed specifically focused on inclusion and creativity to support people within the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

name: Creative Writing Club
description: The Creative Writing Club serves to provide UIUC students an environment in which they can express themselves creatively, hone their craft, and find like-minded individuals to help them grow as creators and as people in general.

name: Cricket Club of Illinois
description: The Club’s objective is to increase awareness and understanding of the game of Cricket on and around the campus of University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, provide opportunities to play the game of Cricket both recreationally and competitively on and around the campus of UIUC, and develop relationships with cricketing organizations and bodies, both within and outside of the state of Illinois.

name: Criminal Law Society
description: The objective of this organization is to: provide the students enrolled at the University of Illinois College of Law with insight about Criminal Law and the Criminal Justice System and to provide students with opportunities to network, communicate, and interact with individuals working or with experience within the Criminal Legal System.

name: Crisis Nursery Student Initiative
description: The Crisis Nursery Student Initiative is dedicated to raising funds and providing support to enhance the well-being of children and their families at Crisis Nursery Urbana, a vital organization situated within our Urbana-Champaign community at 1309 W Hill St, Urbana, IL 61801. Our primary objectives are twofold: to extend our support to Crisis Nursery Urbana and to empower students to emerge as leaders and advocates within their community.

name: Crop Sciences Graduate Student Organization
description: The Crop Sciences Graduate Student Organization (CSGO) seeks to provide social events for interaction between, and to develop educational opportunities for, graduate students within the Department of Crop Sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

name: Cross Country Club
description: The Illinois Cross Country Club was created as a competitive group of athletes that aim to be the top cross country club in the nation. To reach this goal, the Club competes nationally against other top clubs when possible, including at NIRCA Regionals and Nationals for Cross Country and at NIRCA-sponsored meets or races with other NIRCA teams for Cross Country. The Club also competes against varsity squads from D-I, D-II, D-III, and NAIA schools as preparation for those major races.

name: Crossway
description: Crossway is a Korean Christian college organization for those students interested in exploring a faith- based youth ministry. Crossway is the college group of the Korean Church of Champaign Urbana at UIUC. We gather weekly to worship, praise, and to share personal stories and learn from church pastors.

name: Cru
description: The purpose of the Chapter, as articulated in the Charter, is to build movements of people who are transformed by Jesus Christ. The student-led movement seeks to introduce students to Jesus Christ, help them to grow in their faith, encourage them to live life passionately under the lordship of Christ, and inspire commitment to advancing the purposes of God in the world.

name: CSC
description: Chinese Soccer Club (CSC) is a soccer-centered organization that serves as a shelter for people who love soccer but do not find peers to share their values with. By holding events and activities mainly in, but not limited to soccer, CSC is devoted to creating a sense of home for all the members and getting more people involved with this warm community.

name: CU College Age
description: CU College Age serves as a premier group within the UIUC campus to help college students find good and healthy community that can pursue God while also walking through life together. A safe place to be valued, seen and known. CU College Age is affiliated directly with CU Church, a church located in the Urbana-Champaign community. Due to this church affiliation, CU College Age also serves as way to connect students on campus with a church in their local community.

name: Dance2XS at UIUC
description: It shall be the purpose of Dance2XS at UIUC to create a welcoming space for students who want to further their dance training (rehearsals, choreography, workshops/intensives…), performance experience, as well as share their love of hip-hop dance with fellow student dancers.

name: Dance2XS Caliente
description: Mission Statement: The Mission of Dance2xsCaliente is to promote the art of Latin dance and create community around the art. Our organization strives to showcase Latin dance to all those on campus and to the surrounding community. We want to show our dedication and love for dance through performative showcases and workshops. .

name: Dance2XS LUXE
description: As Dance2XS LUXE, our mission is to cultivate a powerful community of dancers who train in stiletto heels at an intense, industry-driven commercial level. We are committed to developing unapologetic confidence, technical precision, performance excellence, and professional discipline. Through rigorous training, innovative choreography, and a supportive yet challenging environment, we empower dancers to refine their artistry, elevate their presence, and prepare for real-world opportunities in the commercial dance industry. Our team stands for strength, individuality, and elevated professionalism

name: Dancing Illini
description: The purpose of this organization is to promote social and ballroom dancing and provide community opportunities and lessons for social and ballroom dancing.

name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Society
description: The purpose of this organization shall be ● Encourage club members to proceed with various artificial intelligence-related projects. ● Organize a community for those interested in data science and artificial intelligence. ● Provide members opportunities to share insights and academic sources. ● Provide members opportunities to readily find project teammates. ● Assist club members to prepare for data-related competitions.

name: Data Science Development Group
description: Data Science Development Group (DSDG) is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing interdisciplinary applications of data science through collaborative projects, professional consulting, and academic engagement. Our mission is to empower students to explore real-world data challenges across diverse domains, foster leadership and technical excellence, and build meaningful connections with industry and academia.

name: Deeper Life Campus Fellowship
description: The DLCF, affiliated with the Deeper Life Bible Church, has a divine mandate and mission to win, build and commission students and staff of UIUC to be their best for the our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. It is an interdenominational fellowship, embracing campus Christians who share the same doctrinal belief irrespective of their denominations and affiliations.

(b) Particularly to build up the membership, ideals, spirit, organization, and physical equipment of this chapter so that affiliation therewith shall ever be regarded as an honor and privilege of which only the finest men are worthy. name: Delta Delta Delta Sorority
description: The Purpose of Delta Delta Delta (hereinafter at times referred to as “Fraternity) is to establish a perpetual bond of friendship among its members, to develop a stronger and more womanly character, to broaden the moral and intellectual life, and to assist its members in every possible way. name: Delta Delta Sigma
description: The mission of Delta Delta Sigma is to provide its members the resources, mentorship, and community needed to succeed as a pre-dental student.

name: Delta Gamma Sorority
description: The objects of this chapter shall be those expressed in the Constitution of Delta Gamma Fraternity, “to foster high ideals of friendship among women, to promote their educational and cultural interests, to create in them a true sense of social responsibility, and to develop in them the best qualities of character.”

name: Delta Kappa Delta Sorority, Inc.
description: Delta Kappa Delta Sorority, Inc. commits itself to the fostering of a united sisterhood, the development of indomitable spirit, the betterment of the community through humanitarian services, and the education of ourselves and others about the Indian sub-continental culture. Furthermore, we dedicate ourselves to personal, cultural enrichment through the awareness and preservation of our traditions and morals.

name: Delta Kappa Epsilon : Delta Pi
description: DKE strives to develop a culture and an expectation of​ undergraduate​ chapters who perform in the top tier of fraternities at their institutions​;​ and a vibrant network of ​alumni who are motivated to stay involved with the fraternity after graduation. We will do this by providing our undergraduates with the leadership​ skills, and the operational resources they need, to excel in today’s Greek environment; and by developing alumni networking programs which are relevant and engaging, and are beneficial to both alumni and undergraduates.

name: Delta Phi Omega Sorority, Inc.
description: The purpose of Delta Phi Omega shall be to foster unity among South Asian Women, build community awareness, and gain a greater understanding of oneself and others. The sorority aspires to instill leadership traits, excel in all academic endeavors, to encourage an active relationship between the sorority and its respective university and shall do so with the utmost compassion, dignity, and fortitude.

name: Delta Sigma Pi Business Fraternity
description: Delta Sigma Pi is a professional business fraternity organized to foster the study of business in universities; to encourage scholarship, social activity and the association of students for their mutual advancement by research and practice; to promote closer affiliation between the commercial world and students of commerce, and to further a higher standard of commercial ethics and culture and the civic and commercial welfare of the community.

name: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc Alpha Nu Chapter
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is an organization of college-educated women committed to the constructive development of its members and to public service with a primary focus on the Black community.

name: Delta Upsilon
description: Building Better Men

name: Delta Zeta
description: The mission of Delta Zeta is to inspire action and impact lives globally through philanthropy, service, and scholarship.

name: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Graduate Student Advisory Council University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign
description: ChBE GSAC serves as the representative body of graduate students that acts as a liaison between the graduate students and the department administration. We organize social, professional, outreach, and recruitment events including the Graduate Research Symposium, professional networking, welcome week, and recruitment weekends. We provide bonding opportunities for students and foster a sense of community.

name: Design Build Fly
description: Design Build Fly focuses on the design, fabrication, and testing of a remote-controlled aircraft that will ultimately fly in the annual AIAA Design Build Fly Competition.

name: Design For America at UIUC
description: Design For America at UIUC is a design organization that advocates for interdisciplinary applications and awareness of human-centered design. Its core mission involves the development and implementation of projects with various partners utilizing the human-centered design process and the teaching of human-centered design principles to members of the club and greater community.

name: Design Innovation Illinois
description: Our mission is to build a diverse community of innovative designers and thinkers that work across disciplines and at the forefront of technology. We believe in the transformative power of design and that everyone should have the opportunity to practice it and grow their creative potential.

name: Design Movement
description: Design exists to help students come to know Jesus personally, grow in their faith, and be empowered to share God’s love with their families, communities, and the world. This mission is rooted in the Great Commission from Matthew 28:18–20, where Jesus calls his followers to make disciples and teach others to walk with Him.

name: Destino
description: A growing movement of Latino students experiencing fellowship, spiritual multiplication, and being sent out into the world. We value faith, growth, and fruitfulness in a compassionate community committed to being culturally connected Christ-centered leaders.

name: Detonation Propulsion at Illinois (DPI)
description: Detonation Propulsion at Illinois advances student-led work in detonation-based propulsion at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. We give students the opportunity to develop experimental propulsion hardware, from initial research through manufacturing and testing. Our first project, Resonance, is a liquid oxygen and methane rotating detonation rocket engine targeting approximately 2 kN of thrust with active water cooling. name: Deutschklub at Illinois
description: It shall be the mission of Deutschklub to be inclusive of all willing participants, regardless of formal German enrollment, and to explore the multi-faceted culture of the German-speaking world without prejudice.

name: Dheem
description: UIUC Dheem is the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s first competitive Indian classical dance team, featuring the dance forms of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi. In the past years, UIUC Dheem has been growing as a dance team that strives to continue our traditional heritage of Indian classical dance forms. We hope to continue to grow as a team and to use the beauty of Indian classical dance to express our own contemporary lives and culture.

name: Disability Law Society
description: The mission of the Disability Law Society (DLS) is to advance accessibility on campus and in the legal field and share resources and opportunities for students interested in the field of disability law.

name: Diverse Curlz

name: Divine Youth Associates
description: Our primary purpose is to bring like-minded youth together to a selfless and open atmosphere to learn more about our culture and history. Our secondary purpose is to help our members leave the organizing as better people than when they entered.

name: DIY Illini
description: DIY ILLINI serves to provide an open community for U of I students to discuss Do-It-Yourself (DIY) desktop design. We are providing a Peer-to-Peer platform for students who are interested in building Customized DIY ILLINI Computers (PC). This platform is to provide solutions (including consultation, recommendation, and tutoring) for 1) students who want to learn PC building skills and build Customized PCs themselves and 2) students who have PC building experiences and would like to help build for others. name: Documentary Club at UIUC
description: The Documentary Club at UIUC serves as to educate members on the documentary making process, as well as provide practical experience in making films in a collective, aiming to share films with the public.

Publish at least one high-quality, peer-reviewed issue each academic year that highlights undergraduate research, reviews, and commentary in biosciences, contributing to the broader scientific community and promoting academic excellence. iii. We share upcoming Go events and competition in the club channel.

description: The purpose of Gospel Fellowship is to help people knowing God, loving God and building a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. We offer Chinese Bible Study, Discipleship class, and various trainings to equip God’s servants. We also occasionally provide special gathering events to welcome our new students and visitors.

description: GradBMES will exist to interface between BIOE graduate students and the department, between all graduate students interested in the field of BMES, and between the graduate and undergraduate chapters of the BMES organization. description: We, the members of the Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO), are committed to the principles of participatory democracy. This can only mean our bona fide representation in University governance. Formal recognition of the work of graduate employees generates due respect for our work and, moreover, ensures better working conditions for all of us. This can only enable the University in successfully fulfilling its mission,

name: Graduate Organization for Computational Social Science
description: the Graduate Organization for Computational Social Science is to provide a collaborative space for students interested in computational methods. The organization focuses on informal learning, including Python study sessions, sharing resources, and supporting each other’s research development

name: Graduate Organization of, for and by Latine Students
description: The Graduate Organization for/by/of Latine Students (GOLS) at Illinois represents, empowers, & unites graduate students who identify as Latine, Afro-Latine, or Indigenous to the Americas. GOLS seeks to serve as a space for Latine graduate students to connect through culture, social, professional, and community service-based activities. The organization supports the development of Latine students at Illinois University and encourages civic engagement with issues that impact Latine folks locally, nationally, and internationally.

name: Graduate Philosophy Organization
description: the GPO serves to further the following three functions: 1. Organization of the graduate students for the purpose of communicating with the faculty and university. This is facilitated by the President, the Grad Reps, the GEO Stewards, and various other positions with outreach responsibilities. 2. Foster environment for professional and personal growth of the graduate students. This is facilitated by the organization of Grad Talks, writing and reading groups, as well as other professional and social activities. 3. description: Graduate Students in Ecology & Evolutionary Biology (GEEB) serves to coordinate and unite graduate students from various departments through their interests in ecology and evolutionary biology. Members of GEEB include students from a wide diversity of campus units; we encourage and welcome graduate students from any campus department to participate in GEEB social and academic activities.

name: Graduate Students of French and Italian
description: The Graduate Students of French & Italian serves as the organization to represent the interests of all graduate students affiliated with the Department of French and Italian. GSFRIT also organizes social activities throughout the year to promote aspects of Francophone and Italophone culture for both members of GSFRIT as well as the greater UIUC community on campus. Through this organization, students are encouraged to voice their opinions, participate in a supportive academic community, and be assured that GSFRIT collective decisions are given consideration in the various departmental committe

name: Graduate Women in the Society of Women Engineers
description: The mission of GradSWE is to promote diversity in graduate education in engineering and science to enable innovative and creative solutions to the future technical challenges of society. GradSWE advocates for women and gender minorities in graduate education so that they can confidently excel at the frontier of scientific advancement. A diverse and balanced workforce of individuals with M.S. and Ph.D. degrees is necessary to tackle society’s biggest challenges with innovation and creativity, and GradSWE strives to make this workforce a reality.

name: Grainger ARISE (Academic Redshirt in Science & Engineering)
description: ARISE provides academically talented students from low -income backgrounds support and preparation to successfully earn their engineering degrees from the University of Illinois.

name: Grainger CARE (Center for Academic Resources in Engineering)
description: The Center for Academic Resources in Engineering (CARE) enhances the learning experience for all undergraduate engineering students through academic support, enhancing collaborative learning opportunities, and providing positive influence through peer mentoring.

name: Grainger Engineering Career Services
description: Engineering Career Services (ECS) at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is a dedicated resource within The Grainger College of Engineering that supports engineering students in their career development and connects them with employers seeking top talent.

name: Grainger Engineering First-Year Experience
description: The Grainger Engineering First-Year Experience (GFX) is an interdisciplinary program designed to enhance the learning experience of every first-year student in engineering. Our goal is to support your aspirations by laying a solid foundation for your collegiate career.

name: Grainger Engineering Modeling and Simulations
description: GEMS shall be a non-partisan RSO dedicated to providing education to students of UIUC on how to use various softwares to model and simulate engineering situations. GEMS shall foster an open community with the purpose of establishing inter-organizational collaboration. GEMS shall be committed to aiding partner RSOs through its activities. GEMS leadership shall be dedicated to furthering the missions outlined in the constitution and be held accountable for their actions in this pursuit.

name: Grainger Engineering Student Design Campus
description: Facilitating the mission of its RSOs by fostering a work environment conducive to success. Where engineering comes alive!

name: Grainger Illinois Engineering Ambassadors
description: Sharing our passion and pride, we inspire middle and high school students to challenge conventional ideas about science and engineering. Through communication and leadership, we strive to become world-class engineers and seek to motivate the next generation of engineers to positively impact the health, happiness, and safety of our world.

name: Grainger International Student Community
description: Grainger International Student Community is part of the Engineering Undergraduate Programs Office (UPO) in the Grainger College of Engineering. Located in Access Point (Office 3322) 1304 West Springfield, we provide opportunities to enhance international and domestic student success through academic, professional, student life and leadership development! GISC programs encourage networking with students, faculty, staff, advisors, deans, and administrators in the Grainger College of Engineering and extended University of Illinois community. It also partners with campus-wide liaisons to enhance o

name: Grainger Morrill Engineering Program (MEP)
description: The Morrill Engineering Program empowers African American, Hispanic and Native American engineering students, supports their success as scholars and leverages a community of students, staff and alumni to achieve excellence in engineering. The program hosts activities throughout the year to enhance the student experience and is open to all students who seek its services.

name: Grainger Outreach & Public Engagement
description: The Worldwide Youth in Science and Engineering LEADers program at The Grainger College of Engineering provides opportunities for undergraduate students to develop their leadership and communication skills by mentoring talented and diverse pre-college students interested in STEM. Together they explore engineering and the sciences through hands-on, minds-on activities. WYSE strives to overcome opportunity gaps by providing students from underrepresented populations with opportunities to experience success and to be able to see themselves as future engineers, programmers, mathematicians, and scie

name: Grainger Technology Entrepreneur Center (TEC)
description: TEC helps students and faculty develop an entrepreneurial mindset to improve the world.

name: Grainger Undergraduate Advising [Undergraduate Programs Office]
description: Welcome to the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign's Grainger College of Engineering's Undergraduate Advising page. Here, you will find information to help you succeed as an Illinois engineering student, from before your arrival on campus through your graduation, and everything in between. name: Grainger Women in Engineering
description: The Women in Engineering (WIE) program at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign's Grainger College of Engineering was established in 1993 as an effort to provide support to students as they build community in engineering. WIE's focus on the University of Illinois campus is to provide equity in access and experiences for all interested in studying at The Grainger College of Engineering. To achieve these goals, WIE, offers and/or promotes programs for a variety of students: engineering summer camps for high school students through the WYSE program, orientation camps for all freshman wom

name: Greek InterVarsity Christian Fellowship
description: Greek InterVarsity serves to reach students in Greek life at The University of Illinois and be a spiritual resource to them with the message of Christ. Greek InterVarsity offers spiritual mentorship to students in Greek life and establishes witnessing communities of students in Greek life who follow Jesus as Savior and Lord: growing in love for God, God’s Word, God’s purposes in the world, and God’s people of every ethnicity and culture.

name: Greeks Redefined
description: The purpose(s) of this organization shall be to promote mental health awareness amongst chapters within Fraternity Sorority Affairs at the University of Illinois.

name: Green Leadership Council
description: GLC is a hub to facilitate collaboration & communication between student groups, administration, and community members; spearhead and assist educational programming; and advocate for students’ campus sustainability goals. This role includes the following duties: a. Provide educational programming b. Act as a centralizing entity between sustainability-oriented groups on campus, campus administration, and the community c. Coordinate and promote campus sustainability efforts d. Advocate for students’ campus sustainability concerns

name: Green Street Eats and Culture
description: GSE serves as a community of people committed to exploring the many cultures and cuisines represented on Green Street. A place for people to learn about the diverse campus and culture surrounding UIUC and Green Street, its history and work to improve the Green Street experience.

name: Green Streets
description: Green Streets is an Illinois RSO focused on connecting community members through weekly trash cleanups. We meet every Sunday at Noon, in Anniversary Plaza before moving out in groups to clean up campus. We also spread information about recycling and trash regulations and statistics so community members can make informed environmental decisions.

name: Grupo Illini
description: Mission- the Grupo Illini serves to provide a space for musicians who love Latin music to play and perform together, while sharing a beautiful aspect of the Latinx community with others in or outside the community.

name: Guild of Unpaid Illinois Lawyer Thespians
description: The objectives of this organization are: To create original productions of theatrical work by and from the students of the college of law; To serve the professional development of the fundamental skills of improvisational ability, public speaking, and other interpersonal skills; To generate comradery, collaboration, and teamwork between students of the College of Law; and To enable all students of this college of law artistic expression and creative outlet alongside their peers

name: Habitat for Humanity Campus Chapter
description: The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) Habitat for Humanity Campus Chapter was established in 1992 by a group of motivated students who recognized the need to end substandard housing in Urbana-Champaign. Working closely with our Champaign County affiliate, our goal is to raise awareness about housing insecurity among students and fundraise for an annual sponsorship towards an affordable home in the surrounding community. Over the past 24 years, our chapter has proudly sponsored and actively built 20 Habitat homes, contributed volunteer labor to dozens more, and engaged thousands

name: Hack4Impact UIUC
description: Hack4Impact UIUC believes in technology's potential to empower activists and humanitarians to create lasting and impactful social change. Our mission is to foster the wider adoption of technology as a tool for social impact.

name: Hands of Health
description: handsofhealth serves to enhance hand dexterity and fine motor skills through engaging, hands-on activities that prepare members for careers in medicine, dentistry, and other health professions. We aim to foster a supportive community of pre-health students while making a positive impact through volunteering and philanthropic initiatives

name: Harmony Ballet
description: The purpose(s) of Harmony Ballet is to develop and maintain the traditional art of ballet at a college level in a supportive and welcoming environment. Harmony Ballet will offer a safe, caring, and nonjudgmental setting in which students of all levels help each other reach their ballet goals via technique training, classical variations, social gatherings, fundraising events, and performance opportunities.

name: Healing Everything And Reaching The Soul
description: HEARTS aims to raise medical professionals that are passionate about the lives and emotions of patients. Regardless of the path that an individual chooses to take, a medical professional holds the responsibility of the physical and emotional well-being of patients and their families. Instead of just treating patients as a source of income or customers, HEARTS desires to teach future generations of medical professionals the importance of creating a positive impact through empathy and compassion.

name: Health and Elder Law Society
description: The Health and Elder Law Society seeks to provide education on health and elder law careers and issues and bolster networking and career opportunities for College of Law students interested in health and elder law careers.

We are committed to promoting academic excellence, professional development, and community engagement while advocating for the interests and needs of our graduate students.

name: Health of The Homeless
description: The purpose of the organization shall be: Health of The Homeless’s mission is to provide basic mental/physical health and hygiene necessities to those that can not do it themselves. We also give a helping hand to any student, community member, or group that needs our support.*

name: Health Policy/American Medical Association Interest Group
description: the [RSO] serves to educate and engage students in health policy, advocacy, organized medicine, and physician leadership. The Organization provides opportunities for members to learn about local, state, and national health policy issues; participate in advocacy and resolution-writing; collaborate with physician and community partners; and represent student perspectives through the American Medical Association (AMA), the Illinois State Medical Society (ISMS), and local medical societies.

name: Healthy Smiles
description: Healthy Smiles UIUC serves to ensure awareness regarding oral health to the younger population of Champaign-Urbana through regular classroom visits and organized events to provide for goody bags filled with oral health supplies.

name: Healthy Strides at Illinois
description: Healthy Strides serves to promote physical and mental wellness through easily accessible physical exercise activities while also promoting philanthropic events to advocate for local matters.

We strive to create meaningful opportunities for students to explore healthcare careers while serving diverse and underserved populations. Through community outreach, healthcare education, research initiatives, volunteering, and collaboration with other organizations, HOK works to make a lasting impact both within our community and among future healthcare professionals.

name: Hearts in Practice
description: Our mission is to empower pre-health students to develop cultural competence and meaningful patient connections across diverse backgrounds. Through collaborative initiatives, community engagement, and professional networking, we aim to foster a more inclusive, empathetic, and effective future healthcare workforce.

name: Hellenic Law Student Association
description: The Hellenic Law Student Association serves to cultivate relationships among law students of Hellenic descent. HLSA intends to connect Greek law students and practicing Greek attorneys to foster professional connections, mentorship, and social opportunities. HLSA hopes to honor the members’ Hellenic heritage and teach others the role of Hellenism in the law.

name: Hellenic Student Association
description: The maintenance, promotion, and diffusion of the Hellenic cultural heritage within the University community and in the United States; - The communication of its members with the Hellenic community within the US and the support of common ideals, dreams, and efforts; - The strengthening and promotion of the relations and collaborations among its members through common activities and group events; - Provide support to members of the Association and organize events and activities of general interest to the UIUC community.

description: The purpose of the Her Campus at Illinois organization is to provide an online hub for Illinois‘s women by providing content that is both a resource and a source of entertainment, highlighting campus news, events, interesting students, faculty, alumni, campus photos, and fashion and lifestyle content specifically tailored for women at Illinois. Staff members will gain journalism, marketing, publicity, and digital media experience, and all students at Illinois will gain a new and fun online resource through this online publication.

Our organization is dedicated to fostering a sense of community and belonging among Hindus at UIUC.

description: Hip-Hop Collective at UIUC serves as the premier collaborative space for students interested in the Performing Arts, Hip-Hop music, and Hip-Hop Culture. This includes (but is not limited to): rappers, singers, producers, instrumentalists, sound-engineers, composers, arrangers, dancers, videographers, photographers, DJs, graffiti artists, graphic artists, etc. Our purpose is to create and nurture collaborative recording projects, provide resources for recordings, rehearsals, feedback, and organize performance opportunities for students and UIUC faculty and staff interested in all things hip-hop

description: The purpose of Hip-Notic Dance Team is to provide an outlet for UIUC student performers to be versatile in dance. HSNA will actively seek opportunities to collaborate with other professional nursing

description: Hispanics Far From Home (HFFH) exists to support Hispanic international students as they navigate the challenges of studying abroad. This organization provides a safe and inclusive space where students can share their cultural values, connect with others who speak Spanish, and foster a sense of home away from home. Our goal is to build a community rooted in shared experiences, mutual respect, and celebration of Hispanic culture.

description: HGSA is formed to promote excellence in academic and professional areas and to further the interests of Graduate Students in History at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.

description: Hive Society Improv serves as the University of Illinois' long-form school of improv. Hive seeks to educate improvisers of all experience levels and maintain a welcoming, inclusive, passionate, and safe environment for all students to learn and perform improv. To successfully coach less experienced improvisers, a new team or “NewBee team” is created with each held audition. Over time, this creates a network of teams stratified by years of experience on Hive. description: The Hoeft Technology & Management (T&M) Program at the University of Illinois bridges the gap between traditional engineering and business education by offering a unique curriculum to a select group of highly qualified business and engineering undergraduates. The T&M Program is a joint venture between the College of Engineering and Gies College of Business and works closely with its corporate affiliate partners to build tomorrow's leaders of the innovation economy.

description: The Hologram Vocaloid Concert Collective is an organization that serves the Vocaloid community at UIUC. Our mission is to foster a vibrant community around Vocaloid by hosting events and creating concerts reminiscent of those from Japan. We seek a hybrid position between an engineering and recreational organization, empowering our members to develop their skills in electronics, programming, and hardware design, while enjoying the novelty of Vocaloid for the UIUC community.

name: Hong Kong Student Association
description: HKSA strives to promote intercultural understanding and appreciation of Hong Kong.

name: Horticulture Club
description: The advancement of knowledge and the development of the professional background of its members.The fostering of good fellowship among students and faculty. name: Hospitality Management Association
description: Hospitality Management Association serves as the social and experiential association for University of Illinois Hospitality Management students to meet others in the same concentration and make professional connections.

description: The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign HFES Student Chapter, hereinafter referred to as the Chapter, is an affiliate of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society, Inc., a nonprofit corporation chartered by the State of California. Purposes of the Chapter are those set forth in the Articles of Incorporation of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society, Inc., hereinafter referred to as the Society.

Through professional development, networking, and going in depth about Human Resource topics, we strive to ensure our members are prepared for a career in Human Resources or any other related field. name: I-CAUSE
description: The mission of the Illinois-Coalition Assisting Undocumented Students’ Education (I-CAUSE) is to create an alliance of undocumented and ally students at the University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign (UIUC) for representation, resource gathering, and access to postsecondary education. We aim to bring awareness of the undocumented status and create an inclusive climate for undocumented students to voice their concern. We strive to empower the community to become allies and advocate for policy change by sharing testimonies.

name: I-Public Affairs Committee
description: IPAC will provide students with the opportunity to lobby, learn, volunteer for candidates, and garner valuable political and educational experiences regarding the United States-Israel relationship. This organization exists for the purposes of giving students the ability to politically mobilize and educate themselves about the complexities of the American-Israel allyship.

name: If/When/How
description: If/When/How educates, organizes, and supports law students and legal professionals to ensure that a new generation of advocates will be prepared to protect and expand reproductive rights as basic civil and human rights.

description: To unite in fellowship and raise and strengthen our ideals and objectives in order to foster the progress of the members academically, socially, and personally to the end that they will be happy and successful citizens in their communities.

name: Illinakia
description: Our mission is to allow students of Greek descent and students interested in Greek culture connect with the ancient tradition of Greek Folkloric Dance. Through bi-weekly practices/meetings, we will learn dances from different regions around Greece and learn the history behind each of these dances. We also hope to grow a community around this tradition and hope it will bring to others the joy it has brought to us.

name: Illini 4000
description: Illini 4000 is a nonprofit dedicated to fighting cancer through tangible action. Each year, members bike across the country to raise funds for cancer research and patient support services — along the way, they document the American cancer experience through an initiative called the Portraits Project, sharing the stories of those touched by the disease.

name: Illini ARC Robotics
description: Illini ARC Robotics serves as platform for robotic competitions and academic exchange to stimulate students' interest in robotics through cutting-edge technologies and innovations. It promotes a culture for young engineers that fosters enthusiasm for science and innovation, willingness to share knowledge and practice, development of problem-solving skills, ambition, motivation, and sincerity.

name: Illini Archery Club
description: Illini Archery is a student organization dedicated to making archery accessible, affordable, and enjoyable for all University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign students, regardless of experience level. We provide a welcoming space where students can learn and develop archery skills, build lasting friendships, and enjoy a healthy, active hobby outside the classroom.

name: Illini Automotive Group
description: The purpose(s) of this organization shall be is the premier automotive and modified car enthusiast group @ UIUC! Gearheads of any background can come and chat, go on cruises, and have a good time with fellow enthusiasts. Also, IAG will educate its members on general automotive maintenance and tuning knowledge by participating in automotive events.

name: Illini Autonomous Vehicles
description: IAV's mission is to provide UIUC students with an environment that takes classroom knowledge and builds on it with real world applications in the UAV field. IAV creates a collaborative and educational environment which aims to build the next generation of advanced UAV's and to compete in the annual SUAS(Student Unmanned Aerial Systems) Competition.

name: Illini Awaaz A Cappella
description: Hello! We are Illini Awaaz! As the only South Asian Co-Ed accapella group on campus, our main goals include promoting inclusivity and cultivating a creative environment and outlet for college students. Throughout the year we perform locally at a variety of cultural and music-related events; we also rehearse, participate, and compete in the ASA (Association of South Asian A Capella) circuit during the spring semester. We encourage anyone and everyone to come to auditions during the first week of school and can’t wait to see what the next school year brings us.

name: Illini Badminton Intercollegiate Sports Club
description: Our philosophy is to promote the growth of badminton throughout the community by providing a competitive yet friendly environment for amateurs to play and challenge themselves.

name: Illini Barbell
description: ILLINI BARBELL shall be established to build a better and more unified gym community across strength sports, which includes bodybuilding, powerlifting, and Olympic lifting. ILLINI BARBELL was founded to introduce prospective members to a variety of strength sports in a safe and encouraging learning environment; fostering a community that extends beyond the gym floor.

name: Illini Bass Fishing Club
description: Provide an enjoyable bass fishing experience to those interested students at the University of Illinois. Compete with other collegiate bass fishing clubs and represent the University of Illinois with pride and class. Emphasize the importance of conservation methods, including catch-and-release, to ensure the future success of bass fishing. Expand the knowledge and skills of every bass angler in the club, regardless of their level of expertise. Promote the sport of bass fishing to the campus community of the University of Illinois and to the world in general.

name: Illini Bhangra
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide opportunity and instruction for aspiring dancers at the University of Illinois by encouraging, advancing, and promoting the art of Bhangra through various performances. Their objective is to fuse both modern and traditional elements of Bhangra to create an entertaining and skillful performance and to compete nationally and perform at campus and community events.

name: Illini Blockchain
description: The purpose of this organization is to - form a community of UIUC students to learn about blockchain technology and fintech - work on projects to gain experience in the industry - network with experienced players in the blockchain field - to write and publish quality articles around the field

name: Illini Books to Prisoners
description: IBTP works to connect students to the Champaign-Urbana Books to Prisoners Program and bring awareness to America’s prison systems. The club will organize book drives and fundraising events to receive donations for the program. The club can provide a space to discuss incarceration and its effects on society through guest speakers and different media presentations.

name: Illini Boxing
description: IBC is to teach the fundamentals of boxing as a sport, provide coaching and practice space for all members, build a nationally recognized competitive boxing team, develop a sense of belonging and camaraderie within the club through social events, and attract community members to the club and sport through volunteerism.

name: Illini Brazilian Jiu Jitsu Club
description: We hope to instill the principles of the sport in our members, as we believe the principles of Brazilian Jiu Jitsu promote a healthier lifestyle. These include building relationships between those of all different experiences and backgrounds, living a healthy lifestyle, and having balance.

The industries that we cover include Investment Banking, Accounting, Finance, Consulting, and Private Equity. We are open to all majors within the University of Illinois. We do not want to have a competitive and toxic atmosphere, which is why

name: Illini CHAARG
description: CHAARG at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign is established for the expressed purpose of helping students on UIUC’s campus learn that living a healthy + happy lifestyle is something that is attainable and fun through the resources provided at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and the surrounding area. This RSO is intended for students who are interested in string chamber music or are unable to join the univeristy lead orchestra but don’t want to give up playing their instruments. This RSO is also inteded for students intersted in community service that implements musical performance.

name: Kappa Delta Chi
description: The purpose of Kappa Delta Chi shall be to promote the traditional values of Unity, Honesty, Integrity, and Leadership of its members. An organization dedicated to service for institutions of higher education and underrepresented communities with special emphasis on the Hispanic/Latino population; a servitude based on love and friendship.

description: Section 1. Local Purposes. This Chapter has been established to provide service and assistance to the University of Illinois Band Program. Section 2. National Purposes. This Chapter will also operate in accordance to the national Purposes located in the Preamble of the National Constitution which are as follows: a) To promote the existence and welfare of the college and university bands and to cultivate at large a wholesome respect for their activities and achievements. b) To honor outstanding band members through the privilege of membership extended as a reward for technical achievement and a

name: Kappa Phi Gamma Sorority, Inc.
description: We, the Sisters of Kappa Phi Gamma Sorority, Inc., shall create a Sisterhood directed towards the advancement of women. Kappa Phi Gamma aims to instill integrity of character and trust as components of personality. The Sorority shall encourage bonding of women in order to strengthen Sisterhood. We shall render service to the community and the university, thus supporting the betterment and unification of society. The Sisterhood shall develop leadership skills and high academic standards that follow into the professional world. Kappa Phi Gamma shall promote pride of culture, womanhood, and self.

description: Kappa Phi Lambda Sorority has formed to increase options for the diverse student body of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Our Sorority was established in the Spring of 1995 to pursue cultural awareness. In the midst of multiculturalism, we are here to continue the pursuit for unity and to bring forth the much-needed consciousness of “voices” that need to be heard.

name: Kappa Pi Beta National Fraternity, Inc.
description: As a Brother of Kappa Pi Beta, I will strive hard to further the existence of this great fraternity. I will do my best to bring forth a bond of unity to all of my fellow Brothers that will stand the test of time. Along with the close relationships that are built, I pledge to promote academic excellence, brotherhood, cultural awareness, social mobility, philanthropy, gentlemen values, and respect towards the individual and community. Regardless of the letters I wear, what organizations I am in, or national origin, I will set the example that unity is the ultimate beginning of Brotherhood. I wil

description: Kappa Sigma is a men’s college fraternity. Its goals are many, but all center on the promotion of friendship, loyalty, and brotherly feeling. The objective of this organization is to excel in all phases of Fraternity and student activity at The University of Illinois. To fulfill this objective, the development of scholarship, leadership, community service, social graces, and cultural awareness are encouraged and stressed. One step to achieving the status of a Kappa Sigma is to be a worldly gentleman. It is each member’s duty to work diligently toward these objectives so that few may equal, and

name: Kaugnay – The Filipino Graduate Student Association
description: KAUGNAY of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign serves as an avenue for Filipino, Filipino American, and other interested graduate students to participate in cultural exchange; promote Filipino cultural awareness within the University of Illinois community, to become part of a supportive space for connection, integration, network, and mentorship; and to take part in the advocacy of embodying one’s cultural identity across disciplines through the celebration of Filipino culture, history, and heritage, along with its links to diasporic and Global South identities.
