description: To promote the sport and culture of kendo and further self-improvement through the activity

name: Keramos
description: The main mission of the Illinois Chapter of Keramos is to promote and emphasize scholarship and character in the thoughts of students in ceramics, to stimulate mental development, and to promote interest in the professional aspects of ceramic engineering, technology, and science.

name: Kick Brass - Brass Band
description: Kick Brass – Brass Band (est. ’23) is the First Official Busking (Street Performing) Band of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Kick Brass focuses on providing entertainment to the community while allowing members to grow as people & musicians.

name: Kinesiology Student Association
description: The Kinesiology Student Association (KSA) at the University of Illinois is dedicated to enriching the academic and personal journey of students pursuing careers in the health sciences. Through engaging community service, dynamic social events, and campus-wide health promotion, we create opportunities for students to connect, grow, and thrive. KSA empowers members to explore diverse career paths, build lasting relationships, and contribute meaningfully to a vibrant and supportive kinesiology community.

name: Kingfisher Medievalist Club
description: The purpose of this organization is to promote participation in the research and re-creation of pre-seventeenth century global historical activities such as medieval fencing, armored martial arts, arts, crafts, sciences, and history within a safe environment and an inclusive community among UIUC students.

name: Kings Assembly Redeemed Christian Church of God
description: To help students within the Champaign Community serve and worship God To conduct community involvement - Outreach and Charity outing Observe Prayer meeting and Bible study Conduct Seminars, Teachings, Workshops and Conferences Assist one another academically, morally, and spiritually Provide financial support for students who demonstrate need Organize career development and special skill exhibitions

name: Knowledge Sprout Champaign-Urbana Initiative
description: The Knowledge Sprout Champaign-Urbana Initiative serves to bridge educational gaps by providing resources that support literacy, promote inclusion, and build strong foundations for academic success by writing and producing original books created by RSO members aimed toward elementary school aged children with a goal of providing resources for children undergoing English-acquisition by creating bilingual books for school donation.

name: KOJOBS
description: the KOJOBS serves as the support Korean and Korean American students to create resume, prepare for corporate interviews, and efficient way to network in a professional world.

name: Korean American Student Association
description: The Korean American Student Association (KASA) sets out to create a welcoming and inclusive environment for the Korean American community. We aim to foster meaningful connections between students of our organization to further promote cultural awareness and sensitivity.

name: Korean Art Architecture Design Association
description: The Korean Art • Architecture • Design Association (KARD) serves as a Korean representative of the College of Fine and Applied Arts organization, mainly operating and creating the projects related to the Architecture and the Design.

name: Korean Book Club
description: The Korean Book Club serves as to provide a forum on Korean books for University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign students.

name: Korean Illinois Football Association
description: The Korean Illini Football Association serves as the making league for players and helping Korean people to socialize with other students in the Urbana-Champaign.

name: Korean Jesus-Love Church
description: Korean Jesus-Love Church serves as the campus evangelism where various generations come together, aims to be a warm community of love, community of genuine faith, a community growing as true disciples of Jesus, and a community that does not turn away from the pains of the world.

name: Korean Student Association
description: Korean Student Association is dedicated to make a difference in the Urbana-Champaign community. Our mission is to help Korean students achieve their goals during college years and beyond. We do so by hosting career fairs and providing them with opportunities such as volunteer work or language and cultural diffusion to become active members of the society. We also provide sports and social events for them to enhance interaction with other Korean and non-Korean students. By introducing Korean culture to domestic students, we hope to familiarize domestic students to the culture and to encourage t

name: Korean-American Scientists and Engineers Association
description: As outlined in the University of Illinois Student Code, KSEA will: 1) Share the interests in the same academia especially in Engineering and Science 2) Set up the Networks among the Alumni, the Undergraduate, and the Graduate students

name: Korean-Inspired Community For Kicking Sports
description: KICKS (Korean-Inspired Community for Kicking Sports) is a student-run kicking sports community at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, centered on futsal. KICKS serves to improve individuals' skill sets in futsal and other recreational kicking sports such as Jokgu (foot volleyball), Balyagu (kickball), and Korean-OneBa (the Korean version of Brazilian no bounce). Through a weekly season league with small-sized teams, KICKS aims to create an inclusive, close-knit community where undergraduate and graduate students, and anyone interested in Korean ball-related culture, can connect, compe

name: La Agencia
description: La Agencia is a student-led alliance dedicated to cultivating Latino talent and amplifying our cultural voice across industries. While our roots are in advertising, marketing, and media, we proudly welcome and support Latino students from all majors. This RSO exists to equip Latino students with the tools, confidence, and community to lead and thrive in their chosen fields, while shaping inclusive narratives that reflect the richness of our identities.

name: La Colectiva
description: La Colectiva is an advocacy and activism organization that promotes the awareness and inclusion of Latine social and cultural issues. We strive to provide our community with the tools and resources required to develop our consciousness in order to empower our people and all other communities facing similar forces of oppression. We hope to accomplish this by, creating a space that represents and celebrates people of color on the UIUC campus and beyond.

name: La Fuerza Flamenca
description: La Fuerza Flamenca UIUC serves to create a dance community where individuals can create, explore, and express themselves through flamenco dance, a highly expressive Spanish dance style. LFF is a dance group dedicated to sharing the art of flamenco dance with the UIUC community. In a celebration of all individuals and their unique backgrounds, LFF creates art through classical flamenco dance while fusing other forms and dance styles into choreography. LFF will perform flamenco fusion dance.

name: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Inc.
description: The purpose of LUL is to: 1. Uphold the traditions of the University of Illinois. 2. Improve relations between students and the administration. 3. Aspire to bring men together to pursue the development of fellowship and the unification of the community as a whole. 4. Strive towards the pursuit of academic excellence, community involvement, and cultural awareness. 5. To develop leadership skills amongst students.

name: Labor and Industrial Relations Association
description: The Labor and Industrial Relations Association serves to promote philanthropic engagement, to create unique social experiences for all students in School of Labor and Employment Relations to enjoy, and to build an opportunity to continue to develop professional skills and networking opportunities. Together, the Labor and Industrial Relations Association strives to construct an unforgettable, well-rounded, and rewarding experience for everyone in the School of Labor and Employment Relations.

name: Laboratory Animal Medicine Club
description: The Laboratory Animal Medicine Club serves to provide veterinary students with opportunities to become more knowledgeable about the field of laboratory animal medicine as well as possibly pursuing opportunities within the field. Opportunities include but are not limited to: monthly rounds, networking events, wet-labs, and lunch lectures.

name: Lacuna
description: Lacuna is a literary and arts publication of the Carle Illinois College of Medicine community. As a journal of medicine and the humanities, Lacuna publishes original poetry, visual art, essays, and reflective writing that explore the human experience of medicine — creating space for medical students and faculty to process, express, and share the emotional and artistic dimensions of becoming and being a physician.

name: Lambda Phi Epsilon
description: To guide men on a lifelong discovery of authenticity and personal growth.

name: Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Incorporated.
description: Section 1. The purpose of Lambda Theta Alpha shall be to provide a sisterhood based on Unity, Love, and Respect; to provide social and cultural activities; and to carry on charitable and educational programs to promote leadership, maintain high academic standards; and serve as a voice for the Latino community. Section 2. The principles of Lambda Theta Alpha are Unity, Love and Respect.

name: Lambda Theta Phi Latin Fraternity, Inc.
description: The purpose of Lambda Theta Phi Latin Fraternity, Inc., Beta Sigma Chapter, shall be: to practice Latin unity, respect all cultures and creeds, promote brotherhood, maintain a high standard of learning, develop character, to practice chivalry, uphold dignity, and self-identity, assert positive leadership while serving as role models, and be a source of support for students and professionals by making them aware of their responsibilities to the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign’s multicultural community.

name: LAS Leaders
description: The purpose of the LAS LEADERS shall be: a. To serve as ambassadors for the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences to alumni, faculty, and students. b. To set goals and plans for advancing the student body of the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the University of Illinois. d. To foster standards of excellence within the group and its members. e. To provide leadership experiences to all members. f. To serve as a liaison between students, alumni, facult

name: Latinx in Law
description: We, the members of LIL, are committed to fostering a community for Latino students interested in law by providing a supportive platform for personal and professional growth. Through various events, workshops, and meetings, we aim to equip our members with the necessary tools to succeed in law school and beyond. We recognize the underrepresentation of Latinos in the legal profession and seek to show that there is a place for our community in this field. Our mission is to empower and guide each other to achieve success and make a meaningful impact in the legal industry. By offering a supportive

name: Latinx Law Students Association
description: Section 1: The objectives of this Organization are to: A. Advance the interests of members for issues on and off campus, at the discretion of the Executive Board; B. Host events and career panels at the College of Law that focus on diversity and inclusion; C. Connect members to LLSA alumni and other legal professionals for career development and mentorship purposes; D. Connect 1L members to 2L’s and/or 3L’s for mentorship purposes; and E. Organize events that foster meaningful relationships between members and alumni, including LLSA’s Annual Alumni Reception.

description: We are an organization dedicated to empowering women entering public service and uplifting women in our community through feminism, activism, and sisterhood. We strive to create an inclusive space, bringing women of varying gender identities and backgrounds together. All are welcome! This can include, but is not limited to: Education, Medical Field, Research, Engineering, Law, Politics, Architecture, etc.

We create a supportive community where underclassmen can explore applications of classroom concepts, while upperclassmen provide mentorship, technical insights, and behavioral guidance while building on their own skills. Our focus is on consistent, purposeful practice with Leetcode problems and mutual encouragement, ensuring every member is well-prepared for the industry recruiting process.

name: Left Wing Students for Change
description: Left Wing Students for Change serves as a way for Students to get involved in shaping their communities. This RSO focuses on five main pillars, with all of them playing an integral role. The 1st is to help elect Progressives into all levels of office. The second is to help Champaign-Urbana directly with volunteering and charity. Third, to prepare students for careers in politics through providing access for internships, networking, and resume building. description: The purpose of Legend Dance Company is to provide the students of the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign with an opportunity to seriously dance and choreograph on a team in a non-competitive atmosphere. In addition, we will develop repertoire that will be performed in a show during spring semester of every year.

description: Encourage members to practice music in various fields. ● Share a broad range of musical knowledge. ● Provide members an opportunity to perform in public. ● Support beginners in enhancing their performance techniques. ● Welcome students of all ethnic and cultural backgrounds.

name: Letters of Love UIUC
description: To serve the Champaign and global community through handmade cards and more to bring emotional support and love to children battling cancer and other serious illnesses.

name: LGBTJew
description: The objectives of this organization shall be: 1. To provide resources, support, safe spaces, events, and visibility for LGBTQ+ Jewish persons; 2. To destigmatize LGBTQ+ identity within the Jewish community, and vice versa. 3. To further the education of the larger campus community on the intersection between LGBTQ+ and Jewish identities; 4. To partner with nearby pride and Jewish organizations for the purpose of communal solidarity and effective social action; 5. And to promote and facilitate communication between the Jewish and LGBTQ+ communities on campus.

name: Life Drawing Club
description: The purposes of this organization is to engage both students and the community in life drawing. We aim to create a constructive environment where artists -- beginner or experienced -- can dedicate time to creating figure drawings, still lifes, and improving their technique!

description: The Life-Line Bridge Foundation serves to mobilize students at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign to take action against poverty and humanitarian crises by fundraising, organizing awareness campaigns, and supporting both local and global communities in need. We aim to bridge the gap between resources and underserved populations by promoting empathy, service, and equity.

name: LinguaMed
description: LinguaMed offers students immersive experiences in medical language learning to build cultural competence, strengthen holistic healthcare skills, and support clinics facing language barriers in medical translation. We emphasize fostering a space where cultural connection, appreciation, and education can meet to provide our members of diverse origin and varied second-language speaking ability to find community.

name: Linguistics Student Organization
description: Our mission is to foster community among linguistics graduate students as well as to provide platforms to improve professional skills and conduct and present research in linguistics and related fields.

name: Liquid Rocketry at Illinois
description: The Mission of Liquid Rocketry Illinois is to design, simulate, build, test and launch components of and an actual actively 3-axis controlled, pump-fed, liquid propellent rocket. We aim to do this through participation in collegiate rocketry competitions and safely operating rocket components.

name: Love + Flour Baking Club
description: The mission of the Love + Flour Baking Club is to provide a welcoming and inclusive community for individuals who share a passion for baking. The Club aims to promote the joy of baking, enhance culinary skills, and foster a sense of camaraderie among its members. Through regular meetings, activities, and events, we aim to explore various baking techniques, recipes, and cultures while spreading the love of baking to our local community.

description: The RSO aims to educate students on how to look at the capital markets on a macro perspective. We will educate and train students in knowledge of asset and sector allocation. We will focus mainly on fixed income, commodities and currencies education. We believe there is a big market in the space of macro assets of fixed income, commodities and currencies but there is resources for students to gain education in that space.

description: the Make Your Own World DIY Club DIY Club in UIUC serves to create a place where students can DIY small handicrafts to decorate their lives. This group will not only teach students how to make colorful keychains and beautiful bouquets but also teach about cultures from different parts of the world by making out things in their culture. Finally, we will introduce the effect of materials and techniques on the DIY works.

name: makesmewanna art collective
description: makesmewanna is a student organization focused on bringing sustainable, accessible, and unique art into the Champaign-Urbana community. As young artists, we need a place to experiment and find a community. We’re interested in building symbiotic relationships with the people around us; as much as they are informed by our work, we are informed by their energy. Ultimately, our goal is to make and showcase art that can support both the University and the broader CU community. We want to show how art can act as education, entertainment, and a source for real change, all at once. In other words, we

name: Malaysian Student Association (MaSA)
description: Section 1. To ensure the well-being of Malaysians and create a sense of identity for Malaysians here on campus through holding — Social or cultural events. Professional development initiatives. Mental health interventions. Section 2. To preserve the unique culture of Malaysia and educate the campus community about the cultures and celebrations of Malaysia. Section 3. To act as a medium in promoting the University to other Malaysians.

name: MannMukti
description: MannMukti is an organization that aims to encourage healthy, open dialogue of mental health issues in the South Asian community in an effort to remove stigma, improve awareness and promote self-care. All events and social posts by MannMukti will be delivered to this mission.

name: March of Dimes Collegiate Council
description: The MODCC serves as a dedicated group of students who will locate maternal and fetal-related needs at UIUC (and the greater Champaign-Urbana area) and develop services, education, and events to address them. These activities will be aligned with the mission and research led by the March of Dimes, a U.S. nonprofit organization.

name: Mariachi Alma de la Universidad de Illinois
description: We are Mariachi Alma de la Universidad de Illinois, a vibrant ensemble rooted in the heart of La Casa Cultural Latina at UIUC. As a collective, we are deeply passionate about preserving and promoting traditional Mariachi music, celebrating its rich cultural heritage, and the profound ways it nourishes our almas. We serve to play this genre of music to the CU community, representing the University with pride in our institution and our culture.

name: Matcha Club
description: The Matcha Club serves to cultivate appreciation for matcha tea culture, promote wellness through traditional tea ceremonies, and create a community for students interested in Japanese tea traditions, sustainable practices, and the art of matcha preparation. The club aims to educate members about matcha's history, health benefits, and preparation techniques while fostering connections among students who share a passion for this unique beverage.

name: Material Advantage
description: To serve students interested in materials science by keeping the student body informed of the opportunities available within the field of Materials Science, serve as liaisons between the student body and faculty, and to build a supportive community that promotes the growth of friendships and connections within the MatSE program, between other student organizations, and within the larger community.

name: Mattea's Joy UIUC
description: The Mattea’s Joy UIUC serves to bring joy in the journey of families with hospitalized children via various fundraising and volunteer efforts.

name: Matzahpella Illinois
description: Matzahpella strives to enrich the non-competitive a cappella scene and foster community across campus and the greater Urbana-Champaign area through music that celebrates Jewish culture, identity, and tradition. By sharing the joy of a cappella, we aim to create a welcoming, inclusive space where people of all backgrounds can connect, learn, and celebrate together.

name: MCB Philanthropy
description: The MCB Philanthropy RSO is an organization dedicated to providing Molecular and Cellular Biology students at the University of Illinois opportunities to aid local non-profit organizations through financial contributions. MCB Philanthropy aims to increase student involvement and awareness about local non-profit causes through semi-annual fundraising events.

name: Medical Ethics After Dark
description: Our mission is to cultivate thoughtful dialogue on the ethical dimensions of medicine through shared reading. By engaging with diverse perspectives on healthcare we aim to develop critical thinking, moral reasoning, and empathy among future healthcare professionals and students in general.

name: Medical Students for a Sustainable Future
description: Medical Students for Sustainable Future (MS4SF) at UIUC serves to connect and support medical students interested in sustainability, climate health, and environmental justice. The organization fosters education, community engagement, and student-led initiatives, including research, advocacy, innovation in healthcare, and institutional sustainability efforts, while maintaining an inclusive, low-barrier space for exploration and involvement.

name: Medicine4Youth @ UIUC
description: Medicine4Youth at UIUC aims to bridge the gap between medicine and community accessibility by empowering college students to translate complex medical concepts into engaging, age-appropriate education for younger generations. Through youth-focused outreach, educational innovation, and public health communication, the chapter strives to cultivate the next generation’s curiosity for medicine while developing UIUC students into compassionate and socially aware future healthcare leaders.

name: MedicZero
description: The purpose of MedicZero is to enable bystanders with the confidence to recognize emergencies and initiate care, encouraging the delivery of skillful, evidence-based care by providers, and constructing community paramedicine initiatives to improve the prehospital landscape.

name: MedLaunch
description: The mission of MedLaunch is to foster an environment where students from all disciplines can come together with the CU disability community to design, develop, and deliver projects that allow community members to overcome some barrier to accessibility. MedLaunch combines innovation with human centered design and disability advocacy to create a collaborative environment for students to work on meaningful projects and learn new skills.

name: MEDLIFE UIUC
description: MEDLIFE UIUC, a chapter of MEDLIFE International serving the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign community, is committed to creating and providing sustainable medical, educational, and infrastructural support to empower low-income communities at home in Urbana-Champaign and abroad. This organization accomplishes its mission by engaging students of all socioeconomic backgrounds in the opportunity to travel on MEDLIFE international mobile clinics, volunteer in local projects, and fundraise for local and international projects to serve low-income families. This organization is committed to

name: Menace Ultimate Frisbee
description: The purpose of this team is to grow the sport of ultimate within the community while developing each player on the team to the best of their ability. One of the important goals for this team is to maintain participation and dedication in order to compete at the college level. While winning is not an end in itself, we believe that our players’ efforts to be their best will lead this team to succeed at the competitive level. We expect all players to respect themselves and others, demonstrate loyalty, be good teammates, handle failure like they handle success, have team spirit, have a strong work

name: Mexican Student Association
description: The Mexican Student Association serves to foster dialogue and proactive engagement on political, social, and economic structures that influence both the Mexican community at University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign’s and the broader society. Our mission is to promote and celebrate the rich heritage of Mexican culture through the organization of events and activities that reflect authentic traditions. Additionally, we are committed to supporting students pursuing higher education to enhance the well-being of the Latino community.

name: Mi Pueblo Spanish Conversation Groups
description: Mi Pueblo is a student-run language network created to provide informal opportunities to practice conversational Spanish on campus. Student facilitators arrange and maintain weekly, 1-hour meetings with other students to talk about various topics in Spanish. Through these meetings and participation in cultural events and activities, our goal is to improve participants’ Spanish speaking abilities as well as foster genuine social bonds between members of Mi Pueblo conversation groups and the Latinx and Spanish-speaking communities.

name: Mimosa Dance Crew
description: Our mission is to showcase the diversity and creativity of the dance culture through performances that entertain and inspire. Through our passion for dance, we aim to promote cultural exchange and build meaningful connections within our community.

description: The mission of MANRRS is to develop and empower individuals in agriculture, natural resources, and related sciences by nurturing potential, supporting unique journeys, and connecting members to opportunities that inspire leadership and innovation.

All students are welcome to join the organization.

name: Minority Association of Pre-Medical Students
description: Amongst many of the minority students on various campuses, there is a genuine belief that there are many minority pre-health students on campuses who have the potential to one day be vital parts of the medical field, but need additional support. As an organization, there is the firm belief that with the guidance and resources that minority students can receive from such an opportunity, the extensive process of becoming a pre-health student can and will soon become a mere obstacle that will be overcome amongst all minority students.

name: Minority Business Students Association
description: The Minority Business Students Association (MBSA) is a community of ambitious, driven students who are committed to growing professionally, personally, and together. We create experiences that help our members turn their goals into action, building the skills, connections, and confidence they need to succeed both at Gies and beyond. Our four pillars, Professional, Corporate, Community, and Philanthropy, shape everything we do. Through our Professional pillar, members develop career-ready skills, gain insight into recruiting, and learn from peers who have navigated the same journey. Through our

description: To further the purpose and objectives of the Phi Delta Epsilon Fraternity. To promote and facilitate cooperation and communication between student members and medical professionals in the area. To conduct, sponsor, and participate in such activities as it deems necessary or desirable in accomplishing the foregoing purposes of the organization. To sustain its membership annually by organizing and conducting an annual membership campaign. To provide ample opportunity for members to develop leadership skills by participating in the planning and execution of its activities.

name: Phi Delta Phi - Illini Hall
description: The mission of this organization is to promote the advancement of the highest intellectual, professional, and ethical standards within the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign community. It will be the responsibility of this Hall, and the charge of each of its members, to seek excellence in scholastic and ethical standards towards the achievement of this goal.

name: Phi Eta Sigma National Honor Society
description: We, the members of the Phi Eta Sigma National Honor Society, Inc., promote a higher standard of learning and encourage high scholastic attainment among the freshmen in our institutions of higher learning, do ordain and establish this constitution for the government of our society.

name: Phi Gamma Nu Professional Business Fraternity
description: To be the medium for premiere University of Illinois students to join an organization that is driven to professionalism, dedicated to the community, and devoted to each other.

name: Phi Iota Alpha Fraternity, Inc.
description: The brotherhood comprises undergraduate, graduate, and professional men committed to the empowerment of the Latin American community by providing intensive social and cultural programs and activities geared towards the appreciation, promotion, and preservation of Latin American culture.

name: Phi Kappa Psi
description: Phi Kappa Psi develops members of character by providing them with the proper environment and tools to pursue productive, honorable, and purposeful lives.

name: Phi Kappa Sigma
description: The objects of the Fraternity shall be the promotion of good fellowship and the cultivation of the social virtues among its members; the protection of the just rights and the advancement of the best interests, present and future, individual and collective, of all those who shall be associated together as members of the Fraternity; the encouragement of good scholarship and breadth of training for its members; and cooperation in the educational and cultural programs of institutions of higher education in which Chapters are located.

name: Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity
description: The mission of Phi Kappa Tau is to champion a lifelong commitment to brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership and exemplary character.

name: Phi Kappa Theta Fraternity
description: The mission of Phi Kappa Theta is dedicated to fostering a culture of academic excellence, leadership development, and service to the community, while promoting brotherhood and personal growth among our members.

name: Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia Fraternity
description: The Object of this Fraternity shall be: for the development of the best and truest fraternal spirit; the mutual welfare and brotherhood of musical students; the advancement of music in America and a loyalty to the Alma Matter.

name: Phi Sigma Kappa
description: To promote brotherhood, to stimulate scholarship and to develop character among its members; to assist and further the education of its members by means of endowments, scholarships, or any other means of practical assistance; to inculcate, instill and promote among its members a high degree of morality, culture and fellowship; to charter chapters in colleges and universities; to charter alumni clubs; and to do all things incident to these purposes.

name: Phi Sigma Rho Engineering Sorority
description: Phi Sigma Rho's mission is to promote academic and professional excellence, while also fostering lifelong bonds of sisterhood and high standards of personal integrity, respect, and character.

name: Phi Sigma Sigma
description: Cultivate relationships, secure and provide financial resources for Phi Sigma Sigma sisters to achieve excellence, impact their communities, and change the world.

name: Phi Sigma Tau Honor Society in Philosophy
description: The Illinois Zeta Chapter of Phi Sigma Tau exists to serve as a hub for students who are serious about philosophy. Our mission is to foster a strong intellectual community where students can exchange resources, engage in constructive debate, form study groups, present and critique research, and challenge one another to grow as philosophers. Membership in PST is intended to represent meaningful academic achievement and sustained engagement with philosophy. The chapter provides a space where that work is recognized, respected, and further developed through collaboration with peers. While members

name: Philippine Student Association
description: The Philippine Student Association at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is dedicated to fostering and maintaining relationships through the education and awareness of Filipino identity and culture, developing academic and leadership skills in order to positively impact the self and the community, and provide a welcoming space to explore the unique backgrounds and identities of our community.

name: Philosophy Club
description: Philosophy Club's mission is creating an inviting intellectual community that is open to all students, regardless of their major or philosophical background. The Philosophy Club hopes to be a space for the intellectual development of all of its members through the hosting of weekly discussion meetings, weekly book club meetings, faculty seminars, social events, monthly film screenings, and more.

name: Photon Pictures
description: Our goal is to tell our own stories to the world! We focus on producing films in different genres, including drama, horror, sci-fi, and school romance. Lots of our films have won awards at film festivals. Photon Pictures provides our members with the best creation and learning experiences. We hold regular workshops on scriptwriting, film editing, and directing. We offer professional media production equipment to our members. All the efforts we are making are for the sake of producing better films.

name: Physical Education Teacher Education Club
description: The Physical Education Teacher Education Club aims to build a supportive community for future physical educators by promoting health, fitness and physical activities through community engagement and hands-on learning experiences that prepare students interested in physical education.

name: Physicians for Human Rights
description: Physicians for Human Rights is dedicated to advocating for the end of human rights violations worldwide. Through medical expertise, research, and activism, we strive to expose injustices, support survivors, and promote policies that uphold human dignity and ethical standards in healthcare. Our commitment is to empower physicians and health professionals as advocates for justice, ensuring that medicine serves as a force for human rights and equity across the globe.

name: Physics Outreach and Instruction through New Technologies
description: POINT serves to increase student engagement with science and outreach, and to encourage high school students to pursue AP and college physics classes.

name: Physics Society / Society of Physics Students
description: The mission of SPS national is “The SPS exists to help students transform themselves into contributing members of the professional community. Course work develops only one range of skills. Other skills needed to flourish professionally include effective communication and personal interactions, leadership experience, establishing a personal network of contacts, presenting scholarly work in professional meetings and journals, and outreach services to the campus and local communities.”

name: Pi Beta Phi Sorority
description: The mission of Pi Beta Phi Fraternity for women is to promote friendship, develop women of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service.

name: Pi Kappa Alpha
description: “To advance the educational and literary interests of its members, to promote social intercourse and to make, maintain and uphold a high standard of life and happiness in closer bonds of friendship and brotherly union.”

name: Pi Kappa Phi
description: To create an uncommon and lifelong brotherhood that develops leaders and encourages service to others for the betterment of our communities.

name: Pi Lambda Sigma
description: The purpose of Pi Lambda Sigma is to provide undergraduate students interested in public policy, law, and government with opportunities for professional development, networking, community service, leadership training, and personal education about careers in relation to the government and the legal field in regards to the government. Our goals include the following. Career preparation: Workshops, resume help, speaker events with government officials, policy professionals, or alumni. Networking: Connections with faculty, alumni in law/government, and other students with similar career interests.

name: Pi Rho Omega
description: Pi Rho Omega is a non-profit professional business fraternity established in order to form a brotherhood of like-minded individuals that will enable them to be well-rounded, socially practiced, morally upstanding, professional leaders in the modern business world and in their respective communities.

name: Pious Projects
description: The mission of Pious Projects is to respond effectively to humanitarian causes around the world with trustworthy practice, as well as foster a worldwide sense of community to link between those who are capable and those in need. Pious Projects will be a realm for students to learn more about and contribute to such humanitarian efforts, while also being a part of a campus community.

name: pitchME@UIUC
description: pitchMe@UIUC is focused on bringing pitchMe, an AI-powered public speaking and communication coaching platform from Singapore, to UIUC. Our goal is to help students, particularly those interested in entrepreneurship and technology, strengthen their communication and pitching skills through structured workshops, peer practice, and AI-powered feedback. We exist to bridge the gap between technical brilliance and effective communication, building a community where UIUC students can practice, grow, and pitch with confidence.

name: Pizza.fm
description: The primary purpose of this organization shall be providing a student run, free-format, noncommercial radio station to University of Illinois students. The station also serves to both promote local music to a global audience, and diversify local radio by broadcasting music that is less commercially successful. Lastly, the organization provides opportunities for its members to get involved with music journalism, DIY concerts, and artistic collaborations with other club members.

name: Planned Parenthood Generation Action
description: Planned Parenthood Generation Action at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign exists to educate the university community about reproductive health and rights, to translate increased awareness into pro-choice activism on campus, and to serve as a coalition partner to state, national, and international reproductive rights efforts. Students for PPGA believe in the fundamental rights of every individual to manage their fertility. We support full access to comprehensive reproductive and complementary health care services in settings that preserve and protect the essential privacy and rights o

name: Poetry Club
description: Poetry Club serves to bring together students that enjoy sharing/hearing different perspectives from other students regarding analysis to all types of poetry.

name: Point Four Photography
description: The Point Four Photography, serving the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, is committed to enjoying photography, and teach students to enhance their photography skills. The organization accomplishes its mission by biweekly photoshoots, exhibitions, and seminars.

name: PokeIllini Trainers
description: PokeIllini Trainers serves to provide a welcoming community for students interested in Pokémon. The organization aims to bring students together through social events, video games, the Pokémon Trading Card Game, Pokémon GO, tournaments, discussions, and other Pokémon-related activities. Our mission is to create an inclusive space where students can meet others with shared interests, build friendships, learn from one another, and engage with the Pokémon community on campus.

name: Polish Club Zagloba
description: Polish Club Zagloba is a cultural organization for undergraduate and graduate students at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign who are native Polish speakers, individuals of Polish heritage, and those interested in learning about and interacting with Polish culture.

name: Political Science Graduate Student Association
description: The mission of the PSGSA is to enhance the academic, professional, and social experience of the Illinois Political Science graduate students by: Providing training events, academic resources, and mentorship to graduate students; Organizing social and sports activities; Facilitating channels for feedback and representing graduate students in discussions with the department; Disseminating information about the Graduate Employee Organization (GEO) and university resources; and Working with the department leadership to promote a respectful and uplifting work environment for all graduate students.

name: Pollinator Garden Network
description: Provide students with the opportunity to participate in national restorations, establish access to plants, tools, and other necessary restoration equipment and supplies, educate the student community on pollinators, native plants, and ecological restoration with hands-on experience and through development of guides, and develop transferable skills for members in restoration ecology, environmental science, and native plant-pollinator relationships by cultivating pollinator gardens for students to enjoy across campus

name: Positive Pre-Meds
description: Positive Pre-Meds serves to offer the pre-medical/health students at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign a comforting place to be able to gather with other pre-medical students who may feel overwhelmed and stressed with the pressure that may come with pursuing a path/career in medicine.

name: Post It Forward
description: The Organization shall operate a weekly cycle of reflective prompts, response collection, and scheduled publication across campus residence halls and public campus spaces. Prompts invite brief written reflection on experience, perspective, and advice. Responses are published on designated days each week without identifying information. By making peer reflection visible and low-effort to contribute to, the Organization works to strengthen wellness, self-awareness, and connection among students at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

name: Potted Meat Sketch Comedy
description: Potted Meat Sketch Comedy serves as the University of Illinois’ Sketch Comedy team. We strive to hone our comedic skills in writing, directing, and performing by creating professional, high quality video sketches and giving in person performances of sketches to the community.

name: Power Engineers
description: It shall be the purpose of this organization to provide student inspired events and activities to students in accordance with the Electrical & Computer Engineering Mission.

name: Pre-Anesthesiologist Assistant Association
description: The Pre-Anesthesiologist Assistant Association serves to educate, support and empower students interested in the Anesthesiologist Assistant profession by fostering a community that provides access to mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities and exposure to the field of anesthesia and preoperative care.

name: Pre-Dental Club
description: The Pre-Dental Club is an organization of students dedicated to the field of dentistry. We regularly hold meetings with information regarding applying to dental school, speakers from the dental field, and the tools to succeed. We also organize volunteer events, trips to local offices, dental labs, and dental schools. If you are interested in dentistry get involved!

name: Pre-Genetic Counseling Club
description: The Pre-Genetic Counseling Club serves to create a supportive network of current students, UIUC alumni, current genetic counselors and genetic professionals. Students will explore the field of genetic counseling through educational opportunities, networking events, and advocacy experiences.

name: Pre-Health Latino Undergraduate Society
description: The Pre-Health Latino Undergraduate Society (PLUS) empowers Latino pre-health students at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign by fostering academic success, cultural identity, and community engagement. We are committed to addressing the health needs of Latino communities through advocacy, education, and service.

name: Pre-Health Personal Finance RSO
description: The Pre-Health Personal Finance Club of UIUC serves as a community for students who are interested in personal finance and who are pursuing a Pre-Health pathway. Utilizing University of Illinois resources as well as those obtained externally, the club aims to approach financial literacy from a healthcare-focused perspective, connecting the realities of medical education costs, student loan management, and early-career earnings with budgeting, investing, and long-term financial planning. Through application-based workshops, guest speaker events, and social networking, we hope to better prepare

name: Pre-Health Psychology Association of UIUC (PPA)
description: Pre-Health Psychology Association of UIUC serves as a community for those who are interested in psychology and who are interested in pursuing a Pre-Health Pathway. Utilizing University of Illinois resources as well as those obtained externally, PPA aims to view healthcare from a holistic perspective connecting medical conditions with psychology, neuroscience, cognitive science, and overall mental health. Through application-based workshops, volunteering, and social networking, we hope to better prepare future healthcare providers with the necessary experience and knowledge needed to succeed wi

name: Pre-Law Honors Society: The Order of Prospective Lawyers
description: The University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign Pre-Law Honors Society is a professional law society advancing integrity, compassion and courage through service to the student, the school, the profession and the community.

name: Pre-Medical Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association
description: Pre-Medical APAMSA serves to explore and resolve the unique challenges, obstacles, and responsibilities specific to Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AANHPI) pre-health/health students and health professionals and address health needs specific to Asian Americans, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Island communities through leadership, education, research, and service as further outlined in the Bylaws.

name: Pre-Occupational Therapy Association
description: Pre-Occupational Therapy Association serves as a professional student organization with a focus on preparing students for a career in Occupational Therapy through networking, application assistance, as well as other opportunities to ensure members have a holistic understanding of what Occupational Therapy is.

name: Pre-Optometry Club
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to acquaint its members with the many aspects of the field of optometry, as well as to familiarize them with the colleges of optometry, provide volunteer opportunities, etc.

name: Pre-PA Latino Minority Association
description: Pre-PA Latino Minority Association focuses on encouraging and educating Latino and minority students on the Physician Assistant career path. This is to be done through informational presentations, fundraisers, meetings with PA programs and students, and more. This RSO is open to all students on campus interested in learning more about PA school, planning on attending PA school, or planning on entering any other health related field.

name: Pre-Pharmacy Club
description: The Pre-Pharmacy Club serves to inform Pre-Pharmacy students among the undergraduate population of UIUC about the pharmacy profession and provide an enjoyable and educational environment in which all students can interact, network, and explore many health care opportunities within the Pharmaceutical field

name: Pre-Physical Therapy Club
description: The Pre-Physical Therapy Club at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign is committed to informing students about physical therapy and preparing them for further schooling. Additionally, it provides students with an environment to network with others sharing similar career goals.

name: Pre-Physician Assistant Club
description: The University of Illinois Urbana Champaign's Pre-Physician Assistant club focuses on getting undergraduate students prepared for Physician Assistant school. We meet multiple times every month with meetings that include general information, presentations from PA Program representatives, discussions with actual PA students, and much more. We also organize events for students to earn patient care hours, give back to the Champaign community, socialize with other Pre-PA Students, and fundraise for a variety of charitable causes. Our executive team organizes social, philanthropic, and volunteer opp

name: Pre-Vet Club
description: Our mission is to foster a stronger appreciation and understanding of veterinary medicine and to build a supportive community where students can learn, grow, and form lasting connections.

name: Prime Mergers & Acquisitions
description: The purpose of this organization is to help inform underclassmen of investment banking and expose them to more applied financial concepts.

name: Product Space UIUC
description: Our mission is to provide product strategy consulting services to technology firms. Product Space is a national community and we aim to bring a chapter of Product Space to the UIUC campus. Our core value are community, empathy, and growth. We envision Product Space as an opportunity for emerging professionals to do impactful work at UIUC and beyond. Our members are exposed to a range of topics within product strategy and design consulting while embodying our values of community, growth, and empathy. We understand that success looks different for everyone and welcome diversity of thought.

name: Program for Animal Welfare Through Service at Illinois
description: PAWS serves to provide hands-on opportunities for students looking for animal experience in the Urbana-Champaign area. We foster a community of individuals passionate about animal science welfare and advocacy through active service in local organizations. Our goal is to provide easily accessible animal-related opportunities to all students, regardless of background or experience.

name: Project Code UIUC
description: Explore areas of computer science like app / web development, data science, machine learning, virtual reality / augmented reality, and game development with groups of like-minded peers at UIUC! Join us to work with a Project Manager (PM) and a group of 5-10 students and spend the semester or year working on a project centered around your area of interest (web dev, data science, etc.).

name: Project Gem Cutter
description: Project Gem Cutter will offer a free program that teaches introductory economics, budgeting, investing, retirement planning, debt management, taxes, insurance, and more while connecting students to free programs to teach basic programming skills, coding languages, and applications of coding. This dual-purpose approach will help tie financial literacy to computer sciences and allow for a more modern approach to teaching vital skills in both fields for developing students.

name: Project Guild at the University of Illinois
description: Mission- Project Guild serves as a student-led interdisciplinary organization dedicated to developing, stewarding, and sustaining meaningful student-led initiatives beyond their original teams, semesters, or founders.

name: Project Level the Field: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign Chapter
description: Project Level the Field: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign Chapter serves as a student-led nonprofit organization providing students (mentees), mostly high school students, with high-quality and personable college application resources by our members (mentors). The pillars we follow are knowledge, mentorship, and accessibility. Level the Field provides two comprehensive programs designed to ensure that every student, regardless of their background or socioeconomic status, has access to the resources they need to succeed. name: Project Taqwa UIUC
description: As defined by the national board, Project Taqwa’s primary mission is to address the mental health needs of Muslims in a culturally sensitive and appropriate manner. Project Taqwa UIUC aims to reduce the stigma surrounding mental illness in the Muslim community at UIUC by providing high-quality educational events, resource compilation, media production, and community support efforts.

name: Prospanica
description: Prospanica at University of Illinois at Urbana - Champaign to create an entrepreneurial and professional mindset by inspiring, educating, and practicing. Through academic engagement, technical development, and community involvement, our members prepare to lead in areas like data, design, and technology. As the nation’s first and only fraternity for Information Sciences, we take pride in shaping a collaborative and forward-thinking community for future innovators.

name: Psicología, Avance, Sociedad, Oportunidades, y Servicio
description: PASOS, meaning “steps” in Spanish, represents the journey of growth, progress, and support we take together as students. Our organization is open to all UIUC students, especially those in the College of Liberal Arts & Sciences—who are interested in psychology, mental health, and serving the Latine community. Each letter of PASOS stands for a step: advancing knowledge in Psicología, building Avance through education, strengthening Sociedad (community), creating Oportunidades, and centering Servicio (service). description: Psych Bites serves to: i. Provide opportunities for professional growth of its members through the inclusion of featured guest speakers, writer’s workshops, leadership experiences, and scholarly publication. iii. name: Psychology Research and Community Club
description: Our mission is to provide club members with knowledge about research experience. Through activities conducted in the club, members will familiarize themselves with the process of posing a research question, collecting data, analyzing data, and advocating for mental health. In addition, PRACC will teach members how to hold conversations with empathy using different frameworks of psychotherapy, and we will learn about different areas in psychology research.

name: Psychology Survey Club
description: To create a positive, welcoming, and low-stakes social environment to explore one's psychology oriented interests in a project-based format.

name: Public Interest Law Association
description: The Public Interest Law Association at UIUC aims to provide undergraduate students with the opportunity to coordinate with other undergraduates and provide them a specific connection to PILA nationals' professional networks and resources.

name: Public Interest Law Foundation
description: The Public Interest Law Foundation is an organization of alumni, students and faculty of the University of Illinois, College of Law. It was created fie two purposes: to encourage law students and alumni to pursue public interest law work and help make it financially feasible for them to do so.

name: Public Policy Leaders
description: Public Policy Leaders is an organization at UIUC dedicated to helping students navigate careers in public policy, especially for those not following the traditional law school pathway. Our mission is to provide valuable insights into various policy careers through events with faculty, government officials, and industry professionals. We also offer professional development workshops, including resume writing and LinkedIn sessions, in collaboration with the Career Center. Through hands-on experiences such as case studies, we encourage students to explore critical policy issues, develop leadershi

name: Puerto Rican Student Association
description: Our mission as the Puerto Rican Student Association is to provide a sense of community and uplift Puerto Ricans here on campus. We want to educate, promote, and celebrate Puerto Rican Culture. We hope to bridge the Puerto Ricans across the diaspora to reconnect to our histories, culture, and each other.

description: Shall be to create a conference focused on Electrical and Computer Engineering.

description: The Queer Book Club serves as a place to explore and discuss LGBTQ+ representation in media, with a specific focus on meaningful queer representation in literature. The Queer Book Club strives to provide opportunities for student connection and an accepting and supportive environment to discuss the diversity of queer experiences.

To invite students from across the country to participate in an intercollegiate interactive competition. To facilitate conversation, in regards to Indian culture, that broadens the perspective of our fellow students, faculty, Champaign-Urbana community and students from across the country.

name: Re: verie
description: Re: verie serves as the only non-audition K-pop dance club on campus. Re: verie aims to make dance fun and available to students who may not have the time or years of experience for a competitive team. Additionally, Re: verie provides a space to meet people with similar interests.

Regardless of the student’s current social media footprint, the organization commoves students to use different social media platforms to amplify their following.

name: Recreation, Sport, and Tourism Volunteer Association
description: RSTVA serves to foster a vibrant and inclusive community for students through social, academic, and professional engagement by connecting students with opportunities in the Champaign-Urbana and surrounding communities.

name: Red Bison Ecological Restoration
description: Red Bison is dedicated to championing environmental justice and stewarding healthy ecosystems within and beyond the University of Illinois campus. We strive not only to restore and maintain the natural environment but also to confront systemic issues. Together, we work towards a harmonious coexistence between nature and society, grounded in principles of solidarity and collective action.

name: Reformed University Fellowship
description: Our mission is to grow with students in faith, community, and friendship.

name: Remote Area Medical Chapter at UIUC
description: The RAM Chapter at UIUC serves to reduce pain and ease suffering by offering free, high-quality healthcare to those in need. At the University of Illinois, we strive to be leaders in operating clinics that improve the quality of life by delivering care to impoverished, isolated, and underserved communities.

name: Reproduction and Fertility Initiative (RAFI) UIUC
description: RAFI serves to promote awareness of reproductive and fertility health by conducting research projects and advocacy efforts. We are committed to increasing knowledge on women’s health to bridge the gap between current research and lived experiences of women receiving reproductive healthcare.

name: Retrocomputing and Hardware at Illinois
description: Retrocomputing and Hardware at Illinois serves as the place for enthusiasts of retrocomputing and other old technology at University of Illinois to share, learn, and have fun enjoying the hobby. Our primary topic of focus is computing hardware, but anyone interested in retro audio, video, gaming, and photography will feel right at home in our weekly meetings. For more ambitious members, we undertake projects aimed at repairing and maintaining old hardware for preservation, and we have FPGA projects targeting emulation as a form of enrichment and coursework preparation.

name: Revamp
description: Revamp is a student-run technology consulting club centered around Agentic AI and Data Analytics. The organization exists for two main purposes: to provide consulting services for client projects, and to create educational opportunities for companies and students through application-based pedagogy. Revamp’s mission is to not only leverage the ever-evolving industry by observing and adapting to fast-paced traction of the technological frontiers, but also to give students a nurturing platform to learn industry-grade AI and Data solutions beyond classrooms.

name: Rho Epsilon, Student Real Estate Association
description: The University of Illinois Rho Epsilon Student Real Estate Association offers students a practical, hands-on, experience in commercial real estate. We expose members to diverse career paths within the industry, introduce students to industry specific knowledge, and grow connections with professionals, providing invaluable networking opportunities that enhance their education and future career prospects in Real Estate.

name: Roblox Club at Illinois
description: Roblox Club at Illinois (RCI) serves to provide University of Illinois students with a welcoming community centered around Roblox. The organization offers opportunities for students to socialize, play Roblox games together, participate in group activities and events, and connect with others who share an interest in the platform. RCI exists to create an inclusive and fun campus community where students of all majors, genders, ethnicities, and other backgrounds, can build friendships and engage with Roblox recreationally.

name: Robobrawl
description: The Robobrawl Committee organization aims to foster and serve the robotics community by providing opportunities for students and community members to learn about and participate in combat robotics. Over the course of the year, we host weekly workshops in order to discuss the basics and introduce newcomers to the art of combat robotics. Furthermore we host build sessions exclusively for our members to aid in the construction of their robots with technical support, guidance and materials, as well as free viewing of the 30lb Robobrawl competition. Additionally we provide professional experiences

name: Rocky Horror UIUC
description: Rocky Horror UIUC serves to host semesterly screenings of The Rocky Horror Picture Show (RHPS) on campus. Since the 1970s, theaters have screened RHPS with shadow casts reenacting the film in real time before a lively audience. Rocky Horror UIUC screenings feature a shadow cast performed and put on by students. Students will have the opportunity to be in either/both the cast or/and production team and engage in a collaborative process to host The Rocky Horror Picture Show for our campus community. Our mission is to engage future architects to think critically about locally harvested lumber, hand-crafting, and the principles of sustainability through active project planning and participation. The organization will start with small-scale intervention projects. Root to Roof eventually aims to create quality, energy efficient large-scale solutions to solve for issues of homelessness and poverty in the local area.

name: Rooted at McKinley and Presby
description: We empower students to rise as engaged leaders: cultivating belonging, purpose, and social responsibility through the arts and social justice initiatives at McKinley Foundation, McKinley Memorial Presbyterian Church, and Presby Hall.

name: Roots Reimagined Theater
description: the roots reimagined theater, The purpose of this club is to celebrate and showcase the richness of Black literature, art, and storytelling through the powerful medium of theater. We aim to create a space where students can explore performance, creativity, and expression without needing to major in theater or have prior experience. Our group provides an inclusive and supportive environment that encourages artistic growth, collaboration, and cultural appreciation.
